raw_response:
I've farmed this land in Quzhou my whole life. I know one rotation: winter wheat, then summer maize. My father did it, I've done it for fifty years. I'm not switching now. My legs aren't what they were, but my younger son comes home during planting and harvest to help me. I have about 8 mu — the rest the village collective redistributed to my son's household years ago.

For wheat, I plant every October after the rains, I ask the village machinery cooperative to do the rotary tillage and seeding for me now because I can't manage the tractor myself. I use the improved wheat seed from the township supply station — the varieties they give us are good, better than what I saved myself in the old days. I apply base fertilizer at planting, then top-dress urea at jointing. I water three times: once before winter sets in, once at jointing, once at heading. Two sprays for rust and aphids in spring.

For maize, I direct-seed into the wheat stubble right after June harvest — no tillage, saves money and my back. The hybrid seed from the station is the only kind that makes sense now. One application of fertilizer, one watering if the rains fail in August. Maize mostly takes care of itself here.

I don't experiment at 76. I grow what I know, I spend what I must, I take what the land gives.
